map.基于曝光三角（光圈、快门、ISO）计算曝光值 EV，并提供多组等效曝光组合，方便: Based on the exposure triangle (aperture, shutter, ISO) it computes the exposure value EV and offers several equivalent exposure combinations so photographers can adjust settings freely while keeping the exposure constant.
map.由光圈、快门、ISO 反算曝光值 EV，量化当前光线亮度并匹配对应拍摄场景。: Back out the exposure value EV from aperture, shutter and ISO to quantify the current light level and match it to a shooting scene.
map.换算等效曝光组合：在 EV 不变前提下用互易律交换光圈与快门。: Convert equivalent exposure combinations: with EV fixed, exchange aperture and shutter time using the reciprocity law.
map.用 EV 分级判断环境（晴天下雪到月光夜景），辅助外拍布光与测光表校验。: Use EV levels to judge the ambient light (from bright snow in sunshine to moonlit night scenes), helping with outdoor lighting and meter checks.
map.：EV100 = log2(N² / t)（N 为光圈 F 值、t 为快门秒数）: EV100 = log2(N^2 / t) (N is the aperture F value, t is the shutter time in seconds); including sensitivity, EV = EV100 + log2(ISO / 100). Scene levels: >=15 snow and beach, >=13 bright sunshine, >=11 overcast or open shade, >=9 overcast or bright interior, >=7 normal interior light, >=5 dusk or dim interior, >=3 night street lighting, >=1 moonlight, <1 very dark.
map.：f/8、1/250 s（t=0.004）、ISO 100：EV100 = lo: f/8, 1/250 s (t = 0.004), ISO 100: EV100 = log2(8^2/0.004) = log2(16000) = about 13.97, so roughly EV 14, meaning bright sunshine. Switching to ISO 400: EV = 13.97 + log2(4) = 15.97, so the same settings correspond to a brighter scene at high sensitivity.
map.ISO 不改变实际进光量，但改变“达到合适曝光所需的亮度”。公式中 EV 随 I: ISO does not change the actual amount of light, but it changes the brightness needed for a correct exposure. In the formula EV rises with ISO, meaning the same exposure settings work in darker environments (at the cost of more noise).

map.EV 不变时，开大一档光圈（进光加倍）需把快门时间减半，反之亦然；例如 f/8: With EV fixed, opening the aperture one stop (doubling the light) requires halving the shutter time, and vice versa; for example f/8 at 1/250s and f/5.6 at 1/500s are equivalent exposures (with different depth of field).
